findings.claim: Goal 5 asks for a normalizer plus a per-harness completeness assertion, but the recommended change set silently drops the normalizer and only proposes the assertion.
findings.evidence: Goals #5: "A normalizer plus a per-harness completeness assertion stops `openspec update` from silently dropping a whole tree." Assessment §4 c404: "Prevention: per-harness completeness assertion, so a tree cannot vanish unnoticed" — and §5's open question scopes only the assertion ("assert only that declared harnesses are non-empty, or full per-harness expected counts"), with no explanation for dropping the normalizer half of the goal.
findings.suggested_fix: Either include the normalizer in c404's scope or explicitly state in §4/§5 why the normalizer component is rejected or deferred (e.g., no contract check exists here to normalize for), so the plan stage does not have to guess.

findings.claim: Goal 6's second acceptance criterion — a run through `~/.claude/skills/...` reporting `status: ok` without `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` exported — is absent from the recommended change set.
findings.evidence: Goals #6: "Then reinstall and verify the live installed `preflight-models.sh` contains `resolver_missing`, and that a run through `~/.claude/skills/...` reports `status: ok` without `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` exported." Assessment §4 c405 covers only the first half: "Land to `main`, `update-skill-pack.sh`, verify `resolver_missing` is live." The integration-level check that reproduces the original failure condition (no `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT`) is never carried into any recommended change.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend c405 to include the installed-surface run without `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` asserting `status: ok`, since that is the end-to-end proof the phase exists to deliver.

findings.claim: The assessment asserts a "standing authorization to always commit `.prometheus/` session logs" that appears nowhere in the goals, constraints, or prior handoffs, and blanket-committing logs could conflict with constraint C-02.
findings.evidence: Assessment §2 Routine: "The standing authorization to always commit `.prometheus/` session logs applies." No such authorization is stated in `goals` or `constraints`; meanwhile C-02 requires "No API keys, tokens, or passwords in tracked files," and session logs are exactly the class of artifact that can capture secret values without review.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite the source of the standing authorization or downgrade it to a proposal; in either case require a secrets scan of the 3 session-log files before committing, per C-02.

findings.claim: The diff stat for concern A covers `.opencode` broadly, but `.opencode` also contains non-mirror files (package.json, package-lock.json, plugin.ts, tsconfig.json), so the "70 files are all OpenSpec mirror" characterization is not established by the quoted command.
findings.evidence: Assessment §1.1 quotes `git diff --stat -- .agent .agents .cursor .opencode` → "70 files changed" and concludes all 70 are the mirror upgrade, but the file tree shows `./.opencode/package.json`, `./.opencode/plugin.ts`, `./.opencode/tools`, etc. Only one example file (`.cursor/skills/openspec-explore/SKILL.md`) was actually inspected line-by-line; the composition of the other 69 files is inferred.
findings.suggested_fix: List the 70 changed paths (or at least the non-`skills/` subset under `.opencode`) so c400's "adopt the mirror upgrade" commit does not silently sweep in unrelated tool artifacts.
